html:
A gladiator from Thrace who led the largest slave revolt against the Roman Republic, from 73 to 71 BCE.

Little is known of his early life. Ancient writers say he may have served with the Roman army, deserted or been captured, and was sold to a gladiator school at Capua. In 73 BCE he and about seventy others broke out and camped on Mount Vesuvius. Escaped slaves and poor herdsmen flocked to them, and Spartacus trained them into an army that beat several Roman forces (see Spartacus' slave revolt).

He seems to have wanted to lead his people out of Italy over the Alps, but they turned back south. A deal with pirates to cross to Sicily fell through. Crassus trapped him in the toe of Italy, and in 71 BCE Spartacus died fighting in a final battle in Lucania. His body was never found. Six thousand captives were crucified along the Appian Way.

The sources, Plutarch and Appian, wrote more than a century later. In modern times Spartacus became a hero of the oppressed: Karl Marx admired him, and German socialists named the Spartacus League after him.
